root_cause.text: The MRP vector attribute parser in `mrp_pdu_parse_vecattr()` mishandles `valen`-controlled event decoding across 3-events-per-byte encoding by not decrementing `valen` for the third event, not treating `valen == 0` as a header-only LeaveAllEvent, and not advancing `attrvalue` between event bytes, causing over-consumption and misparsing of subsequent PDU data.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds an early `if (valen == 0) return 0;` because the old code wrongly consumed `FirstValue` when no vector data exists, and inside the loop it newly adds `valen--;` plus `mrp_attrvalue_inc(...)` after the third event, matching the commit message that the old parser otherwise continued past valid events, consumed the next byte spuriously, and reused the wrong attribute value across byte boundaries.

intent_record.intent_summary: Handle zero-length MRP vector attributes as valid LeaveAllEvent-only PDUs by exiting early before parsing absent fields.
intent_record.what: A new conditional check was added after computing `valen` in `mrp_pdu_parse_vecattr()`: if `valen == 0`, the function now returns 0 immediately, along with a comment explaining that this represents a LeaveAllEvent-only VectorAttribute where FirstValue and Vector fields are absent per IEEE 802.1ak.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the parser now treats zero-length vector attributes as valid special-case PDUs and stops further parsing instead of continuing to process missing FirstValue/Vector fields, preventing incorrect access or misparsing when a LeaveAllEvent-only attribute is received.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix vector attribute parsing by decrementing the remaining value count and advancing the attribute-value pointer after each parsed event.
intent_record.what: Inside the loop in mrp_pdu_parse_vecattr(), after parsing each vector attribute event with mrp_pdu_parse_vecattr_event(), the code now decrements valen and advances mrp_cb(skb)->attrvalue by mrp_cb(skb)->mh->attrlen using mrp_attrvalue_inc().
intent_record.how: This makes the parser consume one attribute value entry per processed event so the remaining value count and current attribute pointer stay synchronized while iterating, preventing repeated parsing against the same attribute value and ensuring subsequent events are associated with the correct next attribute data.

Author: David Ward <david.ward@ll.mit.edu>

    net/802: Implement Multiple Registration Protocol (MRP)
    
    Initial implementation of the Multiple Registration Protocol (MRP)
    from IEEE 802.1Q-2011, based on the existing implementation of the
    Generic Attribute Registration Protocol (GARP).
    
    Signed-off-by: David Ward <david.ward@ll.mit.edu>
    Acked-by: Patrick McHardy <kaber@trash.net>
bic_trace_step.reason: The function body of `mrp_pdu_parse_vecattr()` clearly shows the vulnerable event-decoding logic, so the snippet is sufficient. The root-cause conditions are present in this code. First, `valen` is decremented for the first and second event transitions via `if (!--valen) break;`, but after processing the third event there is no decrement at all before the loop repeats. In the shown code: after the third-event block (`vaevents %= __MRP_VECATTR_EVENT_MAX; vaevent = vaevents; mrp_pdu_parse_vecattr_event(app, skb, vaevent);`) control returns to `while (valen > 0)` without reducing `valen`, which matches the described bug of not decrementing `valen` for the third event. Second, the code does not treat `valen == 0` as a header-only LeaveAll case. It does `if (get_unaligned(&mrp_cb(skb)->vah->lenflags) & MRP_VECATTR_HDR_FLAG_LA) mrp_mad_event(app, MRP_EVENT_R_LA);` and then always copies `firstattrvalue` using `skb_copy_bits(... mrp_cb(skb)->mh->attrlen)` and advances `*offset += mrp_cb(skb)->mh->attrlen;` even when `valen` may be zero, so there is no special-case handling for a header-only LeaveAll vector. Third, the parser only advances `mrp_cb(skb)->attrvalue` before decoding the second and third events (`mrp_attrvalue_inc(...)` appears before event 2 and event 3), but there is no increment after processing the third event before the next loop iteration. That means the next byte's first event is decoded against the same attribute value as the previous byte's third event, matching the root cause of not advancing `attrvalue` between event bytes. Together these flaws can cause over-consumption/misparsing of subsequent PDU data. Therefore this initial implementation contains the vulnerable construct and does not yet contain the fix.

Author: David Ward <david.ward@ll.mit.edu>

    net/802: Implement Multiple Registration Protocol (MRP)
    
    Initial implementation of the Multiple Registration Protocol (MRP)
    from IEEE 802.1Q-2011, based on the existing implementation of the
    Generic Attribute Registration Protocol (GARP).
    
    Signed-off-by: David Ward <david.ward@ll.mit.edu>
    Acked-by: Patrick McHardy <kaber@trash.net>
bic_trace_step.reason: The provided function body `mrp_pdu_parse_vecattr()` is sufficient to determine the issue because it contains the full event-decoding loop controlled by `valen`. The vulnerable construct is present. After reading `valen = be16_to_cpu(get_unaligned(&mrp_cb(skb)->vah->lenflags) & MRP_VECATTR_HDR_LEN_MASK);`, the code enters `while (valen > 0)` and decodes three events from each `vaevents` byte. For the first event, it calls `mrp_pdu_parse_vecattr_event(app, skb, vaevent);` but does not decrement `valen` afterward. It only decrements before the second event via `if (!--valen) break;`, and before the third event via another `if (!--valen) break;`. There is no decrement corresponding to consumption of the third event before the next loop iteration, so one event count remains outstanding per byte when three events are processed. This matches the root cause: not decrementing `valen` for the third event. The code also does not treat `valen == 0` as a header-only LeaveAll case. Even when `valen` is zero, it still unconditionally copies the first attribute value and advances the offset: `if (skb_copy_bits(skb, *offset, mrp_cb(skb)->attrvalue, mrp_cb(skb)->mh->attrlen) < 0) return -1;` followed by `*offset += mrp_cb(skb)->mh->attrlen;`. That means a zero-length vector is not handled as header-only and will incorrectly consume bytes. Finally, attribute progression is incomplete: `mrp_attrvalue_inc(...)` is done only before processing the second and third events, but after processing the third event there is no increment before looping to the next event byte. Thus the next byte's first event is parsed against the same `attrvalue` as the prior byte's third event, matching the root cause that `attrvalue` is not advanced between event bytes. Therefore this initial implementation contains the vulnerable parser logic and does not yet include the fix.
